title: Merge Intervals
statement: Given a list of intervals `[start, end]`, merge all intervals that overlap and return the resulting list of non-overlapping intervals that covers the same ranges.

example.why: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap and become [1,6]; the other two touch nothing.

idea: Unsorted, any interval might overlap any other one. **Sort by start time** and overlapping intervals end up next to each other.
Keep the last merged interval. The next interval overlaps it exactly when it **starts no later than the last one ends**.
Overlap → stretch the last interval's end to the larger of the two ends. No overlap → the next interval starts a new group.

complexity.timeWhy: Sorting dominates; the merge pass afterwards is a single O(n) sweep.
complexity.spaceWhy: The result list can hold up to n intervals when nothing overlaps.

steps.text: Our example: **`intervals = [[1,3],[8,10],[2,6],[15,18]]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Sort by start time. Now intervals that overlap sit **next to each other**, so one left-to-right pass is enough.
Start the answer with the first interval [1, 3]. `result[-1]` is always the group we are still growing.
[2, 6] starts at 2, which is **not after** [1, 3] ends (3) — they **overlap**.
Merge: the group's end becomes max(3, 6) = 6. The group is now [1, 6].
[8, 10] starts a **new group**: append it to the result.
[15, 18] starts a **new group**: append it to the result.
All intervals processed. Return the merged list **[[1, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]**.
Done — the answer is **`[[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]`**. [1,3] and [2,6] overlap and become [1,6]; the other two touch nothing.
